summary: The settled way to hand a three-dimensional model from one tool to another. Everything about the shape of a thing and how its surface looks is finished, ratified and in the core: meshes, textures, a physically based material model, animation curves, skinning, morph targets, cameras, metres and a fixed axis convention. Everything about how a thing behaves is not. The whole specification text contains the word physics once, as a made-up name in an example, and the word audio zero times. Extensions carry the rest, so the level here follows a rule: native means the ratified core text, via-extension means a named extension the Khronos board has actually ratified, and partial means a named extension whose draft text is public but which is not ratified. Twenty-seven extensions are ratified, twenty-four from Khronos and three multi-vendor, and KHR_interactivity is among them. Physics and audio are not. One trap for a standards audience: this format has skins and joints but no agreed bone names, so an animation authored for one avatar will not play on another without a convention this specification does not supply.

coverage.note: This is the whole purpose of the format: a single file, plain text or binary, that carries a model between a creation tool and a runtime.

sources.quote: glTF is an API-neutral runtime asset delivery format.

coverage.note: glTF is a format for delivering a model to a runtime; it describes the model and has no feature for tying objects to a sensor, machine controller or building system, which is left to the application that loads it.

sources.title: glTF 2.0 Specification, section 2.1 General
sources.quote: glTF is an API-neutral runtime asset delivery format.

coverage.note: glTF delivers 3D assets to a runtime; it defines no statement of what a person did in a world or with what result, and a learning record would belong to the application or a record standard such as xAPI.

sources.title: glTF 2.0 Specification
sources.quote: glTF is an API-neutral runtime asset delivery format.

coverage.note: glTF is a delivery format for one runtime asset; it defines no host, so exporting or importing a whole place and stating what survives a host closing falls outside it (a host could write glTF files, but the format itself says nothing about that).

sources.title: glTF 2.0 Specification

coverage.note: glTF is an asset format; it carries a model to a renderer that draws it on the device running it, and it defines no server-side rendering or frame streaming.
